questions.stem: The solubility product of AgBr is $4.9 \times 10^{-13}$ at a certain temperature. Calculate the solubility.
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\mathrm{AgBr \rightleftharpoons Ag^+ + Br^-}$; if solubility is S, then $K_{sp} = S \times S = S^{2}$.
Step 2: $S = \sqrt{4.9 \times 10^{-13}} = \sqrt{49 \times 10^{-14}} = 7 \times 10^{-7}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$
Final Answer: (C) $7 \times 10^{-7}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$
Quick Tip: For a 1:1 salt, $S = \sqrt{K_{sp}}$; rewrite the power of 10 as even before taking the root.

questions.stem: Which of the following reagents is used to convert $\mathrm{C \equiv C}$ triple bond to $\mathrm{C = C}$ double bond to give Cis isomer of alkene?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Partial hydrogenation of an alkyne on a poisoned palladium catalyst (Lindlar catalyst, Pd-C poisoned with quinoline) stops at the alkene stage.
Step 2: Both H atoms add from the same side of the triple bond on the metal surface (syn addition), giving the cis-alkene: $\mathrm{R-C \equiv C-R + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd-C/quinoline} \textit{cis}\text{-}RCH=CHR}$.
Final Answer: (B) Pd -C/quinoline
Quick Tip: Lindlar catalyst gives cis-alkene; Na/liquid $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (Birch-type reduction) gives trans-alkene.

questions.stem: Which of the following changes takes place at positive electrode during recharging of lead accumulator?
questions.solution:
Step 1: The positive electrode of a lead accumulator is the $\mathrm{PbO_2}$ plate. On discharge it is reduced to $\mathrm{PbSO_4}$; recharging reverses this.
Step 2: During recharging (electrolysis), the positive electrode is the anode, where oxidation occurs: $\mathrm{PbSO_4 + 2H_2O \rightarrow PbO_2 + SO_4^{2-} + 4H^+ + 2e^-}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{PbSO_4}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{PbO_2}$
Quick Tip: Charging reverses discharge: at the negative plate $\mathrm{PbSO_4}$ is reduced to Pb, at the positive plate it is oxidised to $\mathrm{PbO_2}$.

questions.stem: Identify neutral aminoacid from following list represented by three letter symbols.
questions.solution:
Step 1: A neutral amino acid has one $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ and one $\mathrm{-COOH}$ group. Extra basic groups make it basic; an extra $\mathrm{-COOH}$ makes it acidic.
Step 2: Arg and His have extra basic nitrogen groups (basic), Asp has an extra $\mathrm{-COOH}$ (acidic). Leucine has an alkyl side chain $\mathrm{-CH_2CH(CH_3)_2}$, so it is neutral.
Final Answer: (C) Leu
Quick Tip: Acidic: Asp, Glu. Basic: Lys, Arg, His. Most others are neutral.

questions.stem: Which from following is a weak field ligand?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Spectrochemical series: $\mathrm{I^- < Br^- < Cl^- < F^- < OH^- < H_2O < NH_3 < en < CN^- < CO}$ (EDTA is also stronger than water).
Step 2: Halide ions lie at the weak end; they cause small crystal field splitting. CO is the strongest, while $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and EDTA are stronger than $\mathrm{F^-}$.
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{F^-}$
Quick Tip: Halides are weak field ligands; CO and $\mathrm{CN^-}$ are the strongest.

questions.stem:
Identify the order of following reaction?
$\mathrm{2NO_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2NO_{(g)} + O_{2(g)}}$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Order is the sum of powers of concentration in the experimentally found rate law.
Step 2: For the thermal decomposition of $\mathrm{NO_2}$, rate $= k[\mathrm{NO_2}]^{2}$, so the order is 2.
Final Answer: (C) 2
Quick Tip: Do not confuse with $\mathrm{2N_2O_5 \rightarrow 4NO_2 + O_2}$, which is first order.

questions.stem:
Identify the products of following reaction?
Formaldehyde + Benzaldehyde $\xrightarrow[\text{ii) } \mathrm{H_3O^{+}}]{\text{i) conc. } \mathrm{NaOH}}$ Products
questions.solution:
Step 1: Both aldehydes lack $\alpha$-hydrogens, so conc. NaOH brings about crossed Cannizzaro reaction.
Step 2: Formaldehyde is the more reactive one; it is oxidised to formate while benzaldehyde is reduced to benzyl alcohol: $\mathrm{HCHO + C_6H_5CHO + NaOH \rightarrow HCOONa + C_6H_5CH_2OH}$.
Step 3: Acidification ($\mathrm{H_3O^+}$) converts $\mathrm{HCOONa}$ to HCOOH (methanoic acid).
Final Answer: (C) Methanoic acid and phenylmethanol
Quick Tip: In crossed Cannizzaro, HCHO is always the one oxidised.

questions.stem: What is the coordination number of a particle in simple cubic close packed structure?
questions.solution:
Step 1: In a simple cubic lattice each particle touches 4 neighbours in its own layer, 1 above and 1 below.
Step 2: Coordination number $= 4 + 1 + 1 = 6$.
Final Answer: (C) 6
Quick Tip: Coordination numbers: simple cubic 6, bcc 8, fcc/hcp 12.

questions.stem: Which from following polymers does NOT contain either -COO - or $-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{NH}-$ linkage in it?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Perspex (PMMA) has ester groups $\mathrm{-COOCH_3}$, glyptal is a polyester, and polyacrylamide has amide groups $\mathrm{-CONH_2}$.
Step 2: Thermocol is expanded polystyrene, $\mathrm{[-CH_2-CH(C_6H_5)-]_n}$, a pure hydrocarbon polymer with no ester or amide group.
Final Answer: (D) Thermocol
Quick Tip: Thermocol = polystyrene, an addition polymer of styrene (only C and H).

questions.stem: Which of the following does NOT exhibit haloform reaction?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Haloform reaction needs a $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ group (or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}$ group).
Step 2: Ethanal $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$, propanone $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}$ and butanone $\mathrm{CH_3COC_2H_5}$ have it. Propanal $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$ has no methyl group on the carbonyl carbon.
Final Answer: (B) Propanal
Quick Tip: Ethanal is the only aldehyde that gives the iodoform test.

questions.stem: What is the expected order of basic strength of different compounds from following.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Alkyl groups are electron releasing (+I effect); they increase electron density on nitrogen and make the lone pair more available.
Step 2: The more alkyl groups on N, the stronger the base on the basis of inductive effect (gas phase): $\mathrm{NH_3 < RNH_2 < R_2NH < R_3N}$.
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{NH_3 < R-NH_2 < R_2NH < R_3N}$
Quick Tip: In water, solvation and steric effects change this order (e.g. $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH > CH_3NH_2 > (CH_3)_3N > NH_3}$).

questions.stem: Calculate the change in internal energy of the system if work done by the system is 18 joule and absorbs heat 50 joule in a particular reaction.
questions.solution:
Step 1: First law: $\Delta U = q + W$. Heat absorbed $q = +50\ \mathrm{J}$; work done by the system $W = -18\ \mathrm{J}$.
Step 2: $\Delta U = 50 + (-18) = 32\ \mathrm{J}$
Final Answer: (B) 32 J
Quick Tip: Work done BY the system and heat lost are negative; heat absorbed and work done ON the system are positive.

questions.stem: Equal masses of helium and oxygen are mixed in an empty container at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$. What is the fraction of the total pressure exerted by helium?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Partial pressure fraction = mole fraction. Take mass w of each gas: $n_{He} = \frac{w}{4}$, $n_{O_2} = \frac{w}{32}$.
Step 2: $x_{He} = \frac{w/4}{w/4 + w/32} = \frac{8}{8 + 1} = \frac{8}{9}$
Final Answer: (C) $\frac{8}{9}$
Quick Tip: Use the molar mass of $\mathrm{O_2}$ (32), not of O atoms (16).

questions.stem: What is the number of oxygen atoms bonded to chlorine in its strongest oxoacid?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Acid strength of chlorine oxoacids increases with oxidation state of Cl: $\mathrm{HOCl < HClO_2 < HClO_3 < HClO_4}$, because the conjugate base is more resonance stabilised.
Step 2: The strongest is perchloric acid $\mathrm{HClO_4}$ (Cl in +7), in which Cl is bonded to 4 oxygen atoms (three Cl=O and one Cl-OH).
Final Answer: (D) 4
Quick Tip: More O atoms on Cl means more delocalisation of the negative charge in the anion, hence a stronger acid.

questions.stem: Dissociation constant of 0.01 M weak acid is $10^{-4}$. What is percent dissociation of acid?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Ostwald's dilution law: $\alpha = \sqrt{\frac{K_a}{c}}$
Step 2: $\alpha = \sqrt{\frac{10^{-4}}{10^{-2}}} = \sqrt{10^{-2}} = 0.1$
Step 3: Percent dissociation $= 0.1 \times 100 = 10\%$
Final Answer: (C) $10\%$
Quick Tip: Percent dissociation $= 100\sqrt{K_a/c}$ for a weak acid with small $\alpha$.

questions.stem: Which among the following gases is least adsorbed on solid at similar conditions of temperature and pressure?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Easily liquefiable gases (higher critical temperature, stronger van der Waals forces) are adsorbed more.
Step 2: Critical temperatures: $\mathrm{SO_2}$ (430 K) $>$ $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ (417 K) $>$ $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (406 K) $\gg$ $\mathrm{H_2}$ (33 K). $\mathrm{H_2}$ has the lowest critical temperature, so it is least adsorbed.
Final Answer: (D) $\mathrm{H_2}$
Quick Tip: Extent of physisorption roughly follows the critical temperature of the gas.

questions.stem: Which from following compounds contains complex anions?
questions.solution:
Step 1: When the complex ion is an anion, the metal name ends in '-ate' (cobaltate).
Step 2: Sodium hexanitrocobaltate(III) is $\mathrm{Na_3[Co(NO_2)_6]}$ with anion $\mathrm{[Co(NO_2)_6]^{3-}}$. (B) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]}$ is neutral; (C) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5(H_2O)]I_3}$ and (D) $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}$ contain complex cations.
Final Answer: (A) Sodium hexanitrocobaltate(III)
Quick Tip: '-ate' ending of the metal = anionic complex.

questions.stem: What are the positions of ' $N$ ' atoms present in purine ring of nucleic acids?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Purine is a pyrimidine ring fused with an imidazole ring; it has 4 nitrogen atoms.
Step 2: In standard numbering, N atoms are at positions 1 and 3 (six-membered ring) and 7 and 9 (five-membered ring); C4 and C5 are the fusion carbons.
Final Answer: (D) 1,3,7 and 9
Quick Tip: Pyrimidine has N at 1 and 3; purine adds N7 and N9 (N9 links to the sugar in nucleosides).

questions.stem: Identify the product ' $A$ ' formed in the following reaction.
questions.solution:
Step 1: The skeletal structure is 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_3}$.
Step 2: $\mathrm{Br_2}$ adds across the C=C bond, one Br on each doubly bonded carbon: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3 + Br_2 \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CBr-CHBr-CH_3}$.
Step 3: Product: 2,3-dibromo-2-methylbutane.
Final Answer: (D) 2,3-dibromo-2-methylbutane
Quick Tip: Addition of $\mathrm{Br_2}$ always gives a vicinal dibromide, so mono-bromo options can be ruled out at once.

questions.stem: Rate of the reaction $\mathrm{A + B \longrightarrow}$ product is $3.6 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$ and rate law is $\mathrm{r = k[A][B]^{2}}$. What is rate constant of the reaction if $\mathrm{[A] = 0.2\,M}$ and $\mathrm{[B] = 0.1\,M}$ ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $k = \frac{r}{[A][B]^{2}}$
Step 2: $[A][B]^{2} = 0.2 \times (0.1)^{2} = 2 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{mol^{3}\,dm^{-9}}$
Step 3: $k = \frac{3.6 \times 10^{-2}}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 18\ \mathrm{mol^{-2}\,dm^{6}\,s^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (B) $18\ \mathrm{mol^{-2}\,dm^{6}\,s^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Square [B] before multiplying; the unit for a third order reaction is $\mathrm{mol^{-2}\,dm^{6}\,s^{-1}}$.

questions.stem: Find out the total number of electrons present in 3.2 g methane?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Moles of $\mathrm{CH_4} = \frac{3.2}{16} = 0.2\ \mathrm{mol}$
Step 2: Electrons per $\mathrm{CH_4}$ molecule $= 6 + 4 \times 1 = 10$, so moles of electrons $= 0.2 \times 10 = 2\ \mathrm{mol}$.
Step 3: Number of electrons $= 2 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 1.204 \times 10^{24}$
Final Answer: (B) $1.204 \times 10^{24}$
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and Ne all have 10 electrons.

questions.stem: Which among the following salt turns blue litmus red in its aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Blue litmus turns red in an acidic solution, which is given by a salt of a weak base and a strong acid.
Step 2: $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ comes from $\mathrm{Cu(OH)_2}$ (weak base) and $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ (strong acid): $\mathrm{Cu^{2+} + 2H_2O \rightleftharpoons Cu(OH)_2 + 2H^+}$. $\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}$ is basic; $\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$ and $\mathrm{NaNO_3}$ are neutral.
Final Answer: (A) $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$
Quick Tip: Salts of transition metal cations with strong acids are usually acidic.

questions.stem: Which lanthanoid from following may exhibit +4 oxidation state with $f^{0}$ configuration?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Ce is $[\mathrm{Xe}]\,4f^{1}5d^{1}6s^{2}$. Losing 4 electrons gives $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$ = $[\mathrm{Xe}]\,4f^{0}$, a stable noble gas configuration.
Step 2: $\mathrm{Tb^{4+}}$ is $4f^{7}$ (not $f^{0}$), Eu prefers +2 ($4f^{7}$) and Lu shows only +3 ($4f^{14}$).
Final Answer: (C) Ce
Quick Tip: $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$ ($f^{0}$) and $\mathrm{Tb^{4+}}$ ($f^{7}$) are the common +4 lanthanoid ions.

questions.stem: Which among the following compounds does NOT form intermolecular hydrogen bonding?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Hydrogen bonding needs H attached to a highly electronegative atom (O, N, F) and a lone pair on such an atom.
Step 2: Phenol and butan-1-ol have O-H groups and form H-bonds. Ethoxyethane has an O with lone pairs and can accept H-bonds (e.g. from water). Butane $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3}$ has only C-H bonds and no electronegative atom, so it cannot take part in H-bonding at all.
Final Answer: (B) Butane
Quick Tip: Alkanes interact only by weak London dispersion forces.

questions.stem: What is the common name of Benzene-1,3-diol?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Dihydroxybenzenes: 1,2- is catechol, 1,3- is resorcinol, 1,4- is quinol (hydroquinone). Pyrogallol is benzene-1,2,3-triol.
Step 2: Benzene-1,3-diol (meta) is resorcinol.
Final Answer: (B) Resorcinol
Quick Tip: Order o, m, p = Catechol, Resorcinol, Quinol (C-R-Q).

questions.stem: Identify a medicinal compound having amide linkage.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Paracetamol is N-(4-hydroxyphenyl)acetamide, $\mathrm{HO-C_6H_4-NHCOCH_3}$, which contains the amide group $\mathrm{-NH-CO-}$.
Step 2: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) and methyl salicylate are esters; curcumin has ketone, phenol and ether groups but no N.
Final Answer: (D) Paracetamol
Quick Tip: An amide needs nitrogen; only paracetamol among the options contains N.

questions.stem: Which among the following has highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
Step 1: All are carboxylic acids that form H-bonded dimers, so the boiling point rises with molar mass (larger van der Waals forces).
Step 2: Formic (C1) < acetic (C2) < butyric (C4) < valeric (C5, pentanoic acid). Valeric acid has the highest molar mass.
Final Answer: (B) Valeric acid
Quick Tip: In a homologous series, boiling point increases with chain length.

questions.stem: What is the numerical value of osmotic pressure of 1 M urea solution if numerical value of osmotic pressure of 0.5 M urea solution is ' $x$ '?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\pi = CRT$, so at the same temperature $\pi \propto C$ (urea does not dissociate, i = 1).
Step 2: $\frac{\pi_2}{x} = \frac{1}{0.5} = 2$, so $\pi_2 = 2x$.
Final Answer: (C) $2x$
Quick Tip: Doubling the concentration of a non-electrolyte doubles the osmotic pressure.

questions.stem: Calculate vapour pressure of volatile liquid A at given temperature if mole fraction and vapour pressure of volatile liquid B are 0.4 and 900 mm Hg respectively [ $\mathrm{P_{total} = 600\,mmHg}$ ]
questions.solution:
Step 1: Raoult's law: $P_{total} = x_A P_A^{0} + x_B P_B^{0}$, with $x_A = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$.
Step 2: $600 = 0.6\,P_A^{0} + 0.4 \times 900 = 0.6\,P_A^{0} + 360$
Step 3: $P_A^{0} = \frac{240}{0.6} = 400\ \mathrm{mm\,Hg}$
Final Answer: (D) 400 mm Hg
Quick Tip: Always find the other mole fraction as $1 - x_B$ first.

questions.stem: Identify from following the correct set of thermodynamic conditions for a reaction to be nonspontaneous at all temperatures.
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$; the reaction is nonspontaneous when $\Delta G > 0$.
Step 2: With $\Delta H > 0$ and $\Delta S < 0$, both terms are positive ($-T\Delta S > 0$), so $\Delta G > 0$ at every temperature.
Final Answer: (D) $\Delta \mathrm{H} > 0$ and $\Delta \mathrm{S} < 0$
Quick Tip: $\Delta H < 0$, $\Delta S > 0$: always spontaneous; signs reversed: never spontaneous.

questions.stem: "It is impossible to determine simultaneously the exact position and exact momentum of an electron." This statement is called
questions.solution:
Step 1: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle: $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \geq \frac{h}{4\pi}$, so position and momentum cannot both be known exactly.
Step 2: Pauli, Hund and Aufbau rules deal with filling of electrons in orbitals, not with measurement.
Final Answer: (D) Heisenberg uncertainty principle
Quick Tip: The principle matters only for microscopic particles like electrons.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is false about oxygen and sulphur?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Both have $ns^{2}np^{4}$ (two unpaired p electrons), O is a gas and $\mathrm{S_8}$ is a solid, and $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{H_2S}$ (stronger O-H bond). So A, C, D are true.
Step 2: Oxygen has no d orbitals and is the most electronegative after F, so it cannot show +4 and +6 states (it shows mainly $-2$; +2 only in $\mathrm{OF_2}$). Only sulphur shows +4 and +6.
Final Answer: (B) Oxygen and sulphur show $-2, +4$ and +6 oxidation states.
Quick Tip: The first member of a group (O, N, F) does not show expanded positive oxidation states.

options.text: Atoms of oxygen and sulphur consist two unpaired electrons in valence shell.
Oxygen and sulphur show $-2, +4$ and +6 oxidation states.
Oxygen is gas while sulphur is solid at room temperature.
Hydride of oxygen is more stable than hydride of sulphur.

questions.stem:
Calculate rate constant of a first order reaction having pre exponential factor $1.6 \times 10^{13}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
$(\mathrm{E_a}/2.303\mathrm{RT} = 21)$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Arrhenius equation: $\log k = \log A - \frac{E_a}{2.303RT}$, i.e. $k = A \times 10^{-E_a/2.303RT}$.
Step 2: $k = 1.6 \times 10^{13} \times 10^{-21}$
Step 3: $k = 1.6 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (D) $1.6 \times 10^{-8}$
Quick Tip: $\frac{E_a}{2.303RT}$ is a power of 10; $\frac{E_a}{RT}$ would be a power of e.

questions.stem: What is the difference in molar mass of Undecane and Dodecane?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Undecane $\mathrm{C_{11}H_{24}}$ and dodecane $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{26}}$ are consecutive members of the alkane series; they differ by one $\mathrm{CH_2}$ unit.
Step 2: Molar masses: $11(12) + 24 = 156$ and $12(12) + 26 = 170$; difference $= 170 - 156 = 14\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
Final Answer: (D) $14\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Adjacent homologues always differ by $\mathrm{CH_2}$ = 14 u.

questions.stem: Which cation from following exhibits no magnetic moment?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, where n is the number of unpaired electrons; $\mu = 0$ when n = 0.
Step 2: $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ $3d^{3}$ (n = 3), $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ $3d^{9}$ (n = 1), $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$ $3d^{2}$ (n = 2), $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ $3d^{0}$ (n = 0).
Final Answer: (B) $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$
Quick Tip: $d^{0}$ and $d^{10}$ ions are diamagnetic.

questions.stem: Identify the product when chlorobenzene is heated with nitrating mixture.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Cl deactivates the ring (-I effect) but directs incoming electrophiles to ortho and para positions (+R effect).
Step 2: $\mathrm{C_6H_5Cl \xrightarrow{conc.\ HNO_3 + conc.\ H_2SO_4} \textit{o}\text{-}ClC_6H_4NO_2 + \textit{p}\text{-}ClC_6H_4NO_2}$ (para is the major product).
Final Answer: (C) Mixture of 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene and 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene
Quick Tip: Halogens are the deactivating but ortho/para directing groups.

questions.stem: Which of the following compounds does not exhibit optical isomerism?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Optical isomerism needs a chiral carbon (four different groups).
Step 2: 2-Iodo-2-methylbutane is $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CI-CH_2CH_3}$: C2 carries two identical $\mathrm{CH_3}$ groups, so it is achiral. In the others the C-I carbon has H, I and two different alkyl groups (e.g. 2-iodo-3-methylbutane: H, I, $\mathrm{CH_3}$, $\mathrm{CH(CH_3)_2}$).
Final Answer: (C) 2-Iodo-2-methylbutane
Quick Tip: A tertiary carbon bearing two identical methyl groups can never be chiral.

questions.stem: Calculate $\%$ by mass of a $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ solution that is 67.2 by volume.
questions.solution:
Step 1: '67.2 volume' means 1 L of solution gives 67.2 L of $\mathrm{O_2}$ at STP $= \frac{67.2}{22.4} = 3\ \mathrm{mol\ O_2}$.
Step 2: $\mathrm{2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2}$, so $\mathrm{H_2O_2} = 2 \times 3 = 6\ \mathrm{mol} = 6 \times 34 = 204\ \mathrm{g}$ per litre.
Step 3: Strength $= \frac{204\ \mathrm{g}}{1000\ \mathrm{mL}} \times 100 = 20.40\%$ (taking 1 mL of solution as 1 g).
Final Answer: (B) $20.40\%$ by mass
Quick Tip: Percent strength of $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ $\approx$ volume strength $\times \frac{68}{224}$ = $67.2 \times 0.3036 = 20.4$.

questions.stem: For the cell reaction, $\mathrm{A_{(s)} + B^{+2}_{(aq)} \longrightarrow A^{+2}_{(aq)} + B_{(s)}}$ if equilibrium constant of reaction is $10^{4}$ at 298 K . What is standard emf of cell?
questions.solution:
Step 1: $E^\circ_{cell} = \frac{0.0592}{n}\log K$ at 298 K; here n = 2.
Step 2: $E^\circ_{cell} = \frac{0.0592}{2} \times \log 10^{4} = 0.0296 \times 4$
Step 3: $E^\circ_{cell} = 0.1184\ \mathrm{V}$
Final Answer: (B) 0.1184 V
Quick Tip: Read n from the charge change of the ions (2+ here), not from the coefficients.

questions.stem: What are the compounds used to obtain nylon salt?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Nylon salt is hexamethylenediammonium adipate, the 1:1 salt that is heated to make nylon-6,6.
Step 2: $\mathrm{HOOC(CH_2)_4COOH + H_2N(CH_2)_6NH_2 \rightarrow [H_3N^+(CH_2)_6NH_3^+][^-OOC(CH_2)_4COO^-]}$ (nylon salt).
Final Answer: (C) Adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine
Quick Tip: Nylon-6,6: both monomers have 6 carbon atoms.

questions.stem: Which from following compounds is an example of primary amines?
questions.solution:
Step 1: A primary amine has an unsubstituted $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ group; each 'N-' prefix in the name means one more group on nitrogen.
Step 2: 4-Bromobenzenamine is $\mathrm{Br-C_6H_4-NH_2}$ (1°). N-methylmethanamine $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2NH}$ and N-phenylbenzenamine $\mathrm{(C_6H_5)_2NH}$ are 2°; N-ethyl-N-methylpropan-2-amine is 3°.
Final Answer: (B) 4-Bromobenzenamine
Quick Tip: No 'N-' prefix in the name = primary amine.

questions.stem: Identify the technique used to know binding nature of nanomaterials?
questions.solution:
Step 1: FTIR (Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy) measures absorption by vibrating bonds, so it reveals the bonding/binding nature and functional groups in a nanomaterial.
Step 2: SEM and TEM give size, shape and morphology; XRD gives crystal structure and particle size.
Final Answer: (D) FTIR
Quick Tip: Bonds = IR/FTIR; structure = XRD; morphology = SEM/TEM.

questions.stem: Which from following compounds is obtained when phenol reacts with dilute nitric acid at low temperature?
questions.solution:
Step 1: The -OH group strongly activates the ring and directs to ortho and para positions, so even dilute $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ nitrates phenol at low temperature (about 298 K).
Step 2: $\mathrm{C_6H_5OH \xrightarrow{dil.\ HNO_3} \textit{o}\text{-}O_2NC_6H_4OH + \textit{p}\text{-}O_2NC_6H_4OH}$ (mixture, separable by steam distillation).
Final Answer: (D) Mixture of ortho and para nitrophenols
Quick Tip: Conc. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ gives picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol).

options.text: Mixture of ortho and para nitrophenols

questions.stem: In the equation, $\mathrm{BiO_3^{-} + 6H^{+} + \mathit{x}e^{-} \rightarrow Bi^{3+} + 3H_2O}$ What is the value of $x$ ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: Oxidation state of Bi in $\mathrm{BiO_3^-}$: $b + 3(-2) = -1$, so $b = +5$. It changes to +3 in $\mathrm{Bi^{3+}}$, a gain of 2 electrons.
Step 2: Charge check: left $= -1 + 6 - x$, right $= +3$, so $5 - x = 3$ and $x = 2$.
Final Answer: (A) 2
Quick Tip: Balance charge after balancing atoms to verify the electron count.

questions.stem: The compound forming ccp structure contains $9.6 \times 10^{23}$ atoms. Find the number of tetrahedral voids formed in it.
questions.solution:
Step 1: In a close packed structure, the number of tetrahedral voids $= 2N$ (octahedral voids = N).
Step 2: Tetrahedral voids $= 2 \times 9.6 \times 10^{23} = 19.2 \times 10^{23} = 1.92 \times 10^{24}$
Final Answer: (C) $1.92 \times 10^{24}$
Quick Tip: N atoms in ccp/hcp: N octahedral and 2N tetrahedral voids.

questions.stem: Identify a pair of molecules having similar shapes of both members.
questions.solution:
Step 1: Use VSEPR (bond pairs + lone pairs on the central atom).
Step 2: $\mathrm{H_2O}$: 2 bp + 2 lp, bent; $\mathrm{SCl_2}$: 2 bp + 2 lp, bent. Others differ: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ pyramidal vs $\mathrm{SO_2}$ bent; $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ square planar vs $\mathrm{SF_4}$ see-saw; $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ trigonal bipyramidal vs $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ square pyramidal.
Final Answer: (C) $\mathrm{H_2O, SCl_2}$
Quick Tip: Same number of bond pairs AND lone pairs = same shape.

questions.stem:
Calculate the molality of the solution of nonvolatile solute if it freezes at $-0.36^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
$\left[K_{\mathrm{f}}\ \text{for solvent} = 1.86\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}\right]$
questions.solution:
Step 1: Taking the solvent as water (freezing point $0^\circ\mathrm{C}$), $\Delta T_f = 0 - (-0.36) = 0.36\ \mathrm{K}$.
Step 2: $m = \frac{\Delta T_f}{K_f} = \frac{0.36}{1.86}$
Step 3: $m = 0.1935 \approx 0.193\ \mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (B) $0.193\ \mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: $K_f = 1.86$ is the value for water, which tells you the pure solvent freezes at $0^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

questions.stem: Calculate $\Delta \mathrm{S_{total}}$ for a certain reaction if $\Delta \mathrm{H} = -150\ \mathrm{kJ}$ and $\Delta \mathrm{S} = 32\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ at 300 K .
questions.solution:
Step 1: $\Delta S_{surr} = -\frac{\Delta H}{T} = -\frac{-150000\ \mathrm{J}}{300\ \mathrm{K}} = 500\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$
Step 2: $\Delta S_{total} = \Delta S_{sys} + \Delta S_{surr} = 32 + 500 = 532\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$
Final Answer: (B) $532.00\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$
Quick Tip: Convert kJ to J before dividing by T.

questions.stem: If $\mathrm{E^\circ \left(Cu^{+2}_{(aq)} \mid Cu_{(s)}\right) = +0.34\ V}$. What is potential for $\mathrm{Cu_{(s)} \rightarrow Cu^{+2}_{(aq)}(0.1M) + 2e^{-}}$ at 298 K ?
questions.solution:
Step 1: The given half reaction is oxidation, so $E^\circ_{ox} = -0.34\ \mathrm{V}$.
Step 2: Nernst equation: $E = E^\circ_{ox} - \frac{0.0592}{2}\log[\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}] = -0.34 - 0.0296 \log(0.1)$
Step 3: $E = -0.34 - 0.0296 \times (-1) = -0.34 + 0.0296 = -0.3104\ \mathrm{V}$
Final Answer: (D) -0.3104 V
Quick Tip: For an oxidation half cell, the product ion goes in the numerator of Q, and $E^\circ$ changes sign.

questions.stem: Calculate the edge length of bcc unit cell if radius of a particle present in it is 186 pm .
questions.solution:
Step 1: In bcc, atoms touch along the body diagonal: $\sqrt{3}a = 4r$, so $a = \frac{4r}{\sqrt{3}}$.
Step 2: $a = \frac{4 \times 186}{1.732} = \frac{744}{1.732} = 429.6\ \mathrm{pm}$
Step 3: $429.6\ \mathrm{pm} = 429.6 \times 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{cm} = 4.296 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm}$
Final Answer: (A) $4.296 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm}$
Quick Tip: $r = \frac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$ (fcc), $\frac{\sqrt{3}a}{4}$ (bcc), $\frac{a}{2}$ (sc).
